source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Citrus scab is caused by the fungus Sphaceloma sp. (also classified as Elsinoe sp.), which produces raised, corky, wart-like lesions on leaves and fruit. On the upper leaf surface this shows as small raised yellowish spots; the underside of affected leaves shows rough, brown, scabby lesions. Unlike citrus canker, scab lesions do not have a yellow halo ring around them. The disease develops more heavily in areas with cool, humid conditions.

Control measures given in the source:
1) Prune to open up the canopy -- don't let branches grow too dense -- so air and sunlight can move through the tree.
2) Fungicide spray: copper chloride trihydroxide 85% WP at 45-60 g per 20 L water, or Propineb 70% WP at 30-40 g per 20 L water.
